informal_statement:
Let \(a<b\). Suppose \(A,P\) are continuous on \([a,b]\),
\[
A(a)=V,
\]
and
\[
A(t)<V
\]
on \((a,b)\). Suppose also that for every interior \(t\), there is a real \(d\) with
\[
A'(t)=d
\]
and
\[
P'(t)=td,
\]
both derivatives existing. Then
\[
P(a)<P(b)+b[V-A(b)].
\]
reason: Source `GreatestLevelRoot.lean:49-79`: Both continuity assumptions, the endpoint area equality, interior strict barrier and pointwise variational derivative witnesses are retained; no endpoint derivative is required.
